summary: Mistral released OCR 4, a new version of its document-parsing model that adds bounding boxes, block classification, and confidence scores, supports 170 languages, can run self-hosted in a single container, and is priced at $4 per 1,000 pages via API ($2 with batch discount) or $5 per 1,000 pages via Document AI.

mechanisms.reason: The model is described as compact enough to run in a single container, reducing the hardware footprint required for high-volume document processing compared to prior generations.
mechanisms.quote: As a compact model deployable in a single container, it is suited to both cost-sensitive and high-volume deployments.

categories.reason: OCR 4 and Document AI are being distributed through Microsoft Foundry as part of an ongoing platform partnership, framed by Microsoft as a milestone in that relationship.
categories.quote: The availability of Mistral Document AI with OCR 4 in Microsoft Foundry marks an important milestone in our partnership.

practices.reason: Teams building document ingestion or RAG pipelines could adopt OCR 4 now given stated benchmark wins, new confidence-scored structured output, and published per-page pricing.
practices.quote: Independent annotators prefer OCR 4 over every leading OCR and document-AI system tested, with win rates averaging 72%, alongside the top overall score on OlmOCRBench (85.20).

practices.reason: The detailed breakdown of benchmark scoring artifacts (ground-truth errors, equation segmentation, reading-order mismatches) gives engineers reasons to distrust aggregate OCR benchmark scores and to build their own document-specific evaluations instead.
practices.quote: These benchmarks are directional. All competitor scores reflect internal reproductions. We recommend evaluating on your own documents.

practices.reason: The single API endpoint now branches into pure-extraction versus Document AI modes with different parameters, schemas, and per-image annotation calls, which changes how a pipeline would be wired to the model.
practices.quote: The practical decision rule: if you need raw extracted content, use OCR 4 as-is. If you need the output reshaped into a structured format, annotated with domain-specific fields, or processed with a custom instruction, add the Document AI parameters to the same call.
